overview: Union and State executives, Parliament and State legislatures, Centre-State relations and devolution to local bodies: 56 official questions (2008-2024), the heaviest B-block section (16 in 2019, 10 in 2024). Parliament (19), Centre-State relations (14) and the Union executive (12) dominate. Questions are now mostly 'choose the wrong answer' and statement-based items on procedure fine print (lapse of bills, vetoes, privileges, pardons).

possibility.angle: Union executive: President, PM, Council of Ministers
possibility.what_they_ask: veto types; pardon terms; President acts on advice even in emergency; Art. 53; coalition era and PM's position
Governor's tenure and hold-over; discretion and judicial review; Governor as UT administrator; bills mandatorily reserved
Money Bill features; Zero Hour; financial committees; RS election method and special powers; lapse of bills; whip; public vs private bills; privileges; budget stages
Council composition fractions; Council's delaying power (no joint sitting); Speaker's position during his removal
Sarkaria/Punchhi/Rajamannar recommendations; constitutional vs statutory bodies (ISC, Zonal Councils); Parliament on State List (249, 252, 253); Art. 304(b) sanction; Seventh Schedule entries; AIS

possibility.angle: Devolution of powers and finances to local bodies
possibility.what_they_ask: State Finance Commission role and article; Panchayat revenue sources; property-tax gaps

traps.trap: [Money Bill exception] Ordinary-bill power applied to a Money Bill
traps.spot: Options/statements saying President can return or suspensively veto a Money Bill
traps.fix: Money Bill: President gives or withholds assent; no return for reconsideration
traps.pyq: 'can be ... returned for reconsideration by the President' is not a feature [group1-prelims-2008#82]; 'Suspensive Veto in the case of Money Bills' false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#45]

traps.trap: Lapse rule reversed by House of origin
traps.spot: Statements on which bills lapse when Lok Sabha dissolves
traps.fix: Bills pending in or passed by LS (pending in RS) lapse; RS-originated bills pending in RS, assent-pending and returned bills survive
Inter-State Council = Art. 263; Zonal Councils and water tribunals = statutes of 1956
traps.pyq: Inter-State Council [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#54]; Zonal Council = advisory grouping [group1-prelims-2012#94]

traps.spot: Rajamannar, Sarkaria, Punchhi, Venkatachaliah offered together
traps.fix: Rajamannar 1969 = State autonomy; Sarkaria 1988 = cooperative federalism, ISC; Punchhi 2010 = Governor removal by State legislature, localised emergency
traps.pyq: Cooperative federalism first → Sarkaria [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#30]; Punchhi on Governor → impeachment by State Legislature [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#31]

traps.trap: Fraction altered in a composition rule
traps.fix: MLAs 1/3, local bodies 1/3, graduates 1/12, teachers 1/12, nominated 1/6

traps.spot: State bicameral disagreement options with 'joint sitting'
traps.fix: No joint sitting in States; Council can only delay (3 + 1 months), Assembly prevails

traps.spot: 'During National Emergency the President acquires discretionary powers'
traps.fix: Art. 74(1): President acts on ministerial advice at all times
traps.pyq: That statement is the wrong one [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#41]

traps.fix: Reprieve = stay; respite = lesser sentence for special reason; remission = reduce quantity; commutation = change form
traps.pyq: 'IV III I II' [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#49]; only President pardons a death sentence [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#50]

techniques.name: Bill-type grid
techniques.how: [Money / Finance / Ordinary / Amendment] Keep a 4-row grid: where introduced, President's recommendation, RS power, joint sitting, President's options; test each statement on the grid.
techniques.example: Money Bill: LS only, President's recommendation, RS 14 days, assent/withhold only → option 4 is not a feature [group1-prelims-2008#82]

techniques.name: Article-route map for State List
techniques.how: List every route by which Parliament enters the State List: 249 RS resolution, 250 emergency, 252 two or more States, 253 treaties, 356 President's rule; 254 governs Concurrent conflicts.
techniques.example: 'Absolute freedom' on Concurrent list contradicts Art. 254 → wrong answer [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#58]

techniques.name: Equal / unequal / special for Rajya Sabha
techniques.how: Sort each RS power: equal (ordinary bills, emergencies, reports), unequal (Money Bills, no-confidence), special (249, 312, VP removal start).
techniques.example: Equal status → CAG report and emergency approval; Money Bills unequal, VP removal special → 'II and IV' [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#55]; Art. 249 direction [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#2]

techniques.name: Terminate what? test
techniques.how: Adjournment ends a sitting; prorogation a session (bills survive); dissolution only LS (most bills lapse).
techniques.example: Only 'adjournment sine die = sitting ended indefinitely' survives [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#51]

techniques.name: Hold-over rule
techniques.how: Constitutional heads (President, Governor) continue until the successor takes office; any 'quit immediately' statement is false.
techniques.example: 'Governor shall quit immediately after expiry of term' → the exception [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#39]

techniques.name: Finance-committee trio
techniques.how: PAC, Estimates, COPU are the financial committees; Estimates is LS-only and pre-spending economy.
techniques.example: Estimates Committee → Financial Committees [group1-prelims-2008#74]; fourth member → COPU [group1-prelims-2012#95]

confusions.remember: first hour, in the rules vs right after it, informal (since 1962)
post-mortem of spending (LS + RS) vs economy in estimates (LS only)
Art. 263, PM chairs vs SRA 1956, Home Minister chairs
1988 cooperative federalism, ISC vs 2010 Governor removal, localised emergency
TN 1969 autonomy vs Union 1988 cooperative federalism
private member's bills, outgoing govt vs return once / indefinite delay
stay of execution vs lesser sentence for special reason
ends session, bills live vs ends LS, most bills lapse
minister, Law Ministry drafting vs any non-minister MP
RS 2/3 resolution, national interest vs two or more States request
narrower vs wider; outsiders too can be punished
Art. 163(2) shields discretion vs ordinary executive acts reviewable

anchors: Art. 53 Union executive in President; Art. 74 acts on advice; Art. 79 Parliament = President + two Houses
Art. 111: Money Bill cannot be returned; no time limit → pocket veto
Money Bill: Rajya Sabha 14 days, recommendations only
RS election by STV (Art. 80(4)); only RS for Art. 249 and Art. 312
Legislative Council: 1/3 MLAs, 1/3 local bodies, 1/12 graduates, 1/12 teachers, 1/6 nominated
Art. 156: Governor holds over till successor; Art. 239(2) Governor as UT administrator acts independently
Art. 263 ISC set up 1990 on Sarkaria; Zonal Councils SRA 1956
Art. 304(b) proviso: President's previous sanction for State trade-restriction bills; Art. 255 cures missing sanction
Freedom from arrest: civil cases only, session + 40 days before/after
Art. 243-I / 243-Y: State Finance Commission every five years
checklist: Identify the bill type before judging any veto or RS power.
Constitutional or statutory? Name the article or the Act.
Negative stem: one statement violates a fixed rule (advice, hold-over, fractions).
Commission question: place it in time (1969, 1988, 2010) and recall its signature idea.
Lapse questions: where did the bill originate and where is it pending?
Watch time-sensitive facts (seat numbers changed in 2014).
